sanskrit: ko hi saṃbandhakaṃ ślāghyam īpsitaṃ yaunam īdṛśam atikrāman na tapyeta sākṣād api śatakratuḥ
english: For who would not grieve upon passing up such a praiseworthy and desirable alliance — this very union — even Indra himself, the performer of a hundred sacrifices?

sanskrit: apatyaṃ caitad āryasya yo yuṣmākaṃ samo guṇaiḥ yasya śukrāt satyavatī prādurbhūtā yaśasvinī
english: Moreover, this is the offspring of a noble one who is your equal in virtues — from whose seed the illustrious Satyavati was born.

sanskrit: tena me bahuśas tāta pitā te parikīrtitaḥ arhaḥ satyavatīṃ voḍhuṃ sarvarājasu bhārata
english: By him, dear child, your father has been repeatedly praised; he is worthy of marrying Satyavati among all the kings, O Bharata.

sanskrit: asito hy api devarṣiḥ pratyākhyātaḥ purā mayā satyavatyā bhṛśaṃ hy arthī sa āsīd ṛṣisattamaḥ
english: Even the divine sage Asita was once refused by me; that foremost of sages had ardently sought Satyavati.

sanskrit: kanyāpitṛtvāt kiṃ cit tu vakṣyāmi bharatarṣabha balavat sapatnatām atra doṣaṃ paśyāmi kevalam
english: But as her father I must speak a little, O bull of the Bharatas: I see only one powerful flaw here — the matter of a rival stepmother.

sanskrit: yasya hi tvaṃ sapatnaḥ syā gandharvasyāsurasya vā na sa jātu sukhaṃ jīvet tvayi kruddhe paraṃtapa
english: For if you were the rival of anyone — be he a gandharva or an asura — he could never live happily when you are angered, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: etāvān atra doṣo hi nānyaḥ kaś cana pārthiva etaj jānīhi bhadraṃ te dānādāne paraṃtapa
english: This is the only flaw here; there is no other, O prince. Know this well — good fortune to you — in the matter of giving and receiving, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: evam uktas tu gāṅgeyas tadyuktaṃ pratyabhāṣata śṛṇvatāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ pitur arthāya bhārata
english: Thus addressed, the son of Ganga replied fittingly, in the hearing of the assembled kings, for his father's sake, O Bharata.

sanskrit: idaṃ me matam ādatsva satyaṃ satyavatāṃ vara naiva jāto na vājāta īdṛśaṃ vaktum utsahet
english: "Accept this resolve of mine as true, O best among those who speak truth: neither one born nor yet to be born would dare to speak such words as these."

sanskrit: evam etat kariṣyāmi yathā tvam anubhāṣase yo 'syāṃ janiṣyate putraḥ sa no rājā bhaviṣyati
english: "I will do exactly as you say: whatever son is born of her shall be our king."

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ punar evātha taṃ dāśaḥ pratyabhāṣata cikīrṣur duṣkaraṃ karma rājyārthe bharatarṣabha
english: When he had said this, the fisherman chief spoke to him again, seeking to accomplish a difficult act regarding the kingship, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tvam eva nāthaḥ paryāptaḥ śaṃtanor amitadyuteḥ kanyāyāś caiva dharmātman prabhur dānāya ceśvaraḥ
english: "You alone are the fitting lord of the immeasurably glorious Shantanu, O righteous soul, and you are the master capable of giving away the maiden."

sanskrit: idaṃ tu vacanaṃ saumya kāryaṃ caiva nibodha me kaumārikāṇāṃ śīlena vakṣyāmy aham ariṃdama
english: "But hear this word of mine and this matter too, O gentle one; I shall speak it in the manner of those who guard maidens, O subduer of foes."

sanskrit: yat tvayā satyavatyarthe satyadharmaparāyaṇa rājamadhye pratijñātam anurūpaṃ tavaiva tat
english: "What you have pledged in the assembly of kings for the sake of Satyavati, O you devoted to truth and righteousness, that is entirely fitting for you."

sanskrit: nānyathā tan mahābāho saṃśayo 'tra na kaś cana tavāpatyaṃ bhaved yat tu tatra naḥ saṃśayo mahān
english: "It cannot be otherwise, O mighty-armed one; there is no doubt about that. But as for offspring that might be born of you — there our doubt is great."

sanskrit: tasya tan matam ājñāya satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ pratyajānāt tadā rājan pituḥ priyacikīrṣayā
english: Knowing that to be his concern, the one devoted to truth and righteousness then pledged anew, O king, wishing to do what was dear to his father.

sanskrit: devavrata uvāca dāśarāja nibodhedaṃ vacanaṃ me nṛpottama śṛṇvatāṃ bhūmipālānāṃ yad bravīmi pituḥ kṛte
english: Devavrata said: "O king of fishermen, O foremost of lords, hear this word of mine which I now speak for my father's sake in the hearing of these assembled kings."

sanskrit: rājyaṃ tāvat pūrvam eva mayā tyaktaṃ narādhipa apatyahetor api ca karomy eṣa viniścayam
english: "The kingdom I have already renounced before, O lord of men; and now, for the sake of offspring as well, I make this firm resolve."

sanskrit: adya prabhṛti me dāśa brahmacaryaṃ bhaviṣyati aputrasyāpi me lokā bhaviṣyanty akṣayā divi
english: "From this day forward, O fisherman, I shall live in perpetual celibacy; even without a son, imperishable worlds in heaven shall be mine."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ dadānīty eva taṃ dāśo dharmātmā pratyabhāṣata
english: Vaishampayana said: Hearing these words, his body-hair standing erect with joy, the righteous fisherman replied to him: "I give her."

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe 'psaraso devāḥ sarṣigaṇās tathā abhyavarṣanta kusumair bhīṣmo 'yam iti cābruvan
english: Then the apsaras in the sky, the gods, and the hosts of sages together rained down flowers and cried out: "This one is Bhishma — the Terrible One!"

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pitur arthāya tām uvāca yaśasvinīm adhiroha rathaṃ mātar gacchāvaḥ svagṛhān iti
english: Then, for his father's sake, he said to that illustrious woman: "Mount the chariot, mother; let us go to our own home."

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu bhīṣmas tāṃ ratham āropya bhāminīm āgamya hāstinapuraṃ śaṃtanoḥ saṃnyavedayat
english: Having said this, Bhishma helped that noble lady onto the chariot, came to Hastinapura, and presented her to Shantanu.

sanskrit: tasya tad duṣkaraṃ karma praśaśaṃsur narādhipāḥ sametāś ca pṛthak caiva bhīṣmo 'yam iti cābruvan
english: Kings both assembled together and separately praised that difficult deed of his, and cried out: "This one is Bhishma — the Terrible One!"

sanskrit: tad dṛṣṭvā duṣkaraṃ karma kṛtaṃ bhīṣmeṇa śaṃtanuḥ svacchandamaraṇaṃ tasmai dadau tuṣṭaḥ pitā svayam
english: Seeing that difficult deed done by Bhishma, his father Shantanu, well pleased, himself granted him the boon of death at will.
